dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows what happened and what is to come in the order of time — the releases of a product, the history of an order, the milestones of a plan, the activity on a record — each event with its date, what it was and, where there is more to say, a few lines; it marks which of them are done, which one is under way and which are still ahead without relying on a color; and it shows a long log of one-line events closer together than a plan of five milestones.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a timeline reads: per size, the marker column's box and the text styles of an event's time, title and body; the dot's size and color; the ring's corners and edge; the glyph's size and color; the fill and the mark of the event that is under way; the space between the marker and the event's content; the connector's color, thickness and its distance from the markers it joins; per density, the space between two events; the time's color; and the spaces between a time, a title and a body.
rules: A timeline is a record to read: events in the order of time, each with a time, a title and an optional body. It is an ordered list and nothing in it is pressed.
A procedure a reader works through, numbered, is steps, not a timeline. A timeline has no numbers: its order is time's, and its marker is a dot or a glyph.
Progress through a flow the person is in (a checkout, a set-up wizard) is neither: a timeline's status reports the state of the events, not where the person is, and no event is pressed to go to it.

Give status only where the events have one (a plan, an order's tracking): done, current, upcoming. A log of things that happened has none. A status is drawn as a shape — a check in a ring, a filled circle, an empty ring — and said in words through statusLabel; never rely on the color.
The order is the product's: oldest first or newest first, as the events are given. Hiding old events, loading more and grouping by day are the product's too.

A timeline brings no color for a title or a body: they take the content color of the surface. The time is secondary content; the ring and the connector are the system's one hairline; the one filled marker is the event that is under way.
Use size large on a page whose purpose is reading; medium among controls. Use density compact for a long log of short events.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a dotted rail by hand.

height.$description: The side of the box every marker is centred in, and the diameter of a ring, per size: two more than one line of the body's text at that size (22 and 26 in the default system). The marker column is this wide. The values a set of steps gives its numbered ring, so the two read as one family.

shape.$description: A ring's corners: a circle in the default system. Never larger than half the marker's box. The dot is a circle whatever this says.

color.$description: The ring around a glyph, around a done event's check and of an upcoming event: the system's one hairline. Decorative — the status is in the shape and in words — so it is not held to a contrast.

width.$description: The ring's width, drawn inside the marker's box.

gap.$description: The space between the marker column and an event's content. Every event's content begins at the same edge.

size.$description: The diameter of the dot that marks an event with no status and no glyph, and of the mark inside the filled marker of the event under way: a third of the marker's box at medium, a point on the line rather than a bullet.

color.$description: The color of the dot: secondary content, a mark beside the text and never louder than it.

size.$description: The box of a glyph inside a ring, at both sizes: the smallest step of the icon scale, which leaves the ring clear around it.

color.$description: The color of a glyph inside a ring, the check of a done event included: the dot's color.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows which milestone of a plan, or which stage of an order, is the one under way now, so that a reader finds it at once among the done and the not yet begun.

color.$description: The fill of the marker of the event that is under way: the primary fill, which everywhere in the system says "the one now". The only filled marker, and the only chromatic thing a timeline draws.
The color of the mark or the glyph on that fill.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows that its events are one course of time by a line from each marker to the next; a product with a plainer manner draws none, which is a thickness of zero.

color.$description: The line that joins a marker to the next: the system's one hairline, the ring's color, the same between done and upcoming events. Decorative.

thickness.$description: The connector's thickness. Zero draws no connector.

gap.$description: The space the connector keeps from the box of the marker above it and from the box of the marker below it, so the line and the markers are read as separate marks.

The space between the end of one event and the beginning of the next, per density. Regular is the space prose puts between two blocks in the default system; compact, half of it, is for a long log of one-line events.

typescale.$description: The text style of an event's time, per size: a step under the body's at that size, so the date is found by its place and its quiet color and does not compete with the title.

color.$description: The color of an event's time: secondary content. The only text color a timeline brings.

gap.$description: The space between an event's time and what follows it (the title, or the body where there is no title).

typescale.$description: The text style of an event's title, per size: the heading role whose size is the body's at that size, so a title is told from the body by its weight and not by being larger.

gap.$description: The space between an event's title and its body.

typescale.$description: The text style an event's body takes where nothing inside it sets another, per size: the running text of prose at the same size.

gap.$description: The space between two blocks of one event's body: half the regular space between two events, so what belongs to one event is closer together than two events are.
